incidents.victim: Hundreds of PHP-based websites worldwide, including a European government site and Nintendo services
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed "php2shell") allow full server compromise via a single crafted HTTP request, before any application code runs.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of websites, including a European government site and Nintendo services, were taken offline as a precaution; Unit 42 identified over 22.6 million potentially exposed instances, and Cloudflare and watchTowr reported early in-the-wild exploitation attempts.

incidents.victim: 600+ organizations across critical infrastructure sectors in the Americas, Europe, and Australia
incidents.vector: SafePay actors compromise credentials and exploit known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices to gain network access, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally and disable backups.
incidents.impact: More than 600 victims have been hit since 2024; actors steal data and encrypt systems, pressuring victims into paying ransoms, including by calling them directly.

incidents.victim: At least 15 Argentina-based healthcare organizations
incidents.vector: A Spanish/English-speaking operator ran a purpose-built autonomous AI pentesting harness, using a dual-agent "Supervisor"/"Executor" Claude Code architecture derived from the open-source PentestGPT project, against Argentine healthcare targets.
incidents.impact: Credentials and medical records were exfiltrated from at least one victim organization.

incidents.victim: Government entities in two countries and private-sector organizations in Brazil and the U.S. (biotech, healthcare, food & beverage, retail, technology, and travel sectors)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking operator accessed Claude models via a China-based AI proxy service and built two AI pentesting harnesses granting Claude Code varying levels of autonomy to conduct reconnaissance and intrusions.
incidents.impact: Compromised government entities in two countries and private-sector organizations in Brazil and the United States across more than 20 named targets.

incidents.victim: Several Indonesian government domains, a government domain of another country, and private-sector entities
incidents.vector: A low-skilled Indonesian-speaking actor used 819 AI agent skills, sourced largely from public GitHub repositories, to task Claude Code with conducting intrusion campaigns, periodically intervening to overcome the model's safety guardrails.
incidents.impact: Compromised several Indonesian government domains, a government domain of another country, and multiple private-sector entities despite the actor's limited security expertise.

incidents.victim: A U.S.-based CRM vendor and several private-sector SaaS and data center entities in Russia, Kyrgyzstan, and the U.S.
incidents.vector: A group of Russian-speaking individuals used a single "/pentest-setup" slash command to task Claude Code with a seven-step autonomous workflow covering enumeration, exploitation, and explicit data exfiltration instructions.
incidents.impact: Exfiltrated corporate client data from a U.S.-based CRM vendor and compromised several SaaS and data center entities, plus one government domain of another country.

incidents.victim: Two Indian public universities and an Indian e-commerce site
incidents.vector: An actor using the handle BUGSTER used jailbroken AI assistants, including the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4 and the Cursor IDE, to conduct AI-generated reconnaissance and a WordPress brute-force campaign.
incidents.impact: Exfiltrated a MongoDB database of more than 5,200 student and faculty records containing PII from one university, obtained a valid admin credential at a second, and enumerated an e-commerce site for API tokens, admin emails, and payment merchant IDs.

incidents.victim: Tor network users
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor compromised more than 330 Tor relay servers, infected them with the Ebury Linux malware, and converted them into exit relays to intercept SSH connections and downgrade/sniff unencrypted email traffic.
incidents.impact: More than 10% of Tor exit relays were affected over a three-day period before detection; compromised servers were blocklisted or taken offline in one of the largest security incidents in Tor's history.

incidents.victim: Burger King Japan
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed a server managing the company's smartphone app.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 11.18 million users, including names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, and gender, was stolen.

incidents.victim: Staples
incidents.vector: A Chinese organized crime group gained access to an internal Staples application ("Nexus") and used it to issue fraudulent gift cards.
incidents.impact: Attackers issued more than 15,000 gift cards worth over $5 million for retailers including Target and Sephora, using them to buy electronics shipped to China for resale.

incidents.victim: Zeabur
incidents.vector: A hacker stole environment variables and other account records in the company's second breach of the year, following an August incident involving its AWS backend.
incidents.impact: Records for more than 320,000 accounts, including environment variables, were stolen; the company will shut down entirely at year's end.

incidents.victim: At least 20 Japanese companies and South Korean banks/financial institutions
incidents.vector: An unidentified threat actor used a Chinese AI agent named Artex to conduct automated intrusions.
incidents.impact: At least 20 Japanese companies were hacked, with the same AI agent also used in intrusions against South Korean banks and financial institutions earlier in the month.

incidents.victim: Alternative for Germany (AfD) political party
incidents.vector: A hacker obtained data from the party's web hosting provider.
incidents.impact: 281GB of internal data and email inboxes were leaked, including website databases, internal documents, and email threads containing racist and antisemitic content; the party claims most inboxes were abandoned, though some emails are from this year.

incidents.victim: H2O Retailing (Hankyu Hanshin department stores)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a website operated by department store brand Hankyu Hanshin.
incidents.impact: Data of 1.26 million customers was stolen in the breach.

incidents.victim: LOXONE (German smart home/building automation company)
incidents.vector: Hackers attacked the company's internal IT network over a weekend.
incidents.impact: The company shut down its internal IT network to contain the intrusion; the incident did not spread to customer systems, which run on localized mini-servers.

incidents.victim: Nikkei
incidents.vector: Hackers used stolen credentials to access a cloud server.
incidents.impact: 1.83 million records were stolen in the company's third security breach over the past month.

incidents.victim: Qubic (cryptocurrency platform)
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited wallet seed phrases generated with insufficient randomness on iOS and macOS clients.
incidents.impact: $1.4 million was stolen from user accounts; the platform halted operations and froze about 87% of the stolen funds.

incidents.victim: National Radiocommunications Company (Radiocom), Romania
incidents.vector: A cyberattack hit the state-owned broadcaster's internal IT network.
incidents.impact: The company shut down its email server; the radio/TV broadcast transmission network itself was not affected.

incidents.victim: Ukraine state data-exchange platform
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking threat actor compromised an Elasticsearch server belonging to the platform.
incidents.impact: 6.8 million documents were stolen from Ukraine's state data-exchange platform.

incidents.victim: TeamUpdraft (WordPress plugin developer)
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed the company's backend database and stole customer account information and connection keys.
incidents.impact: Stolen keys were used to connect to customer sites and deploy malicious plugins.

incidents.victim: OVHcloud CLI users
incidents.vector: A hacker compromised a developer's GitHub account and published malicious versions (v0.11.0-v0.15.0) of OVHcloud's command-line tool containing a credential-stealing binary; researchers linked the compromise to the GlassWorm supply-chain campaign.
incidents.impact: The compromised CLI was live for under two hours before being detected and blocked; affected users are urged to rotate all secrets stored on disk.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (MSPs and downstream Microsoft 365 tenants)
incidents.vector: A threat actor obtained a sensitive multi-tenant API secret for ConnectWise's Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application and used it to authenticate directly into customers' Microsoft 365 environments, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: Sign-in activity was observed across nearly 1,000 Entra tenants with more than 300 successful logins; at least 162 tenants were confirmed compromised, with attackers adding backdoor credentials to maintain access.

incidents.victim: Naval shipbuilder, aircraft engine manufacturer, and law enforcement agency (two NATO countries, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Hackers linked to Russia's GRU military intelligence conducted a cyber-espionage campaign targeting defense-sector organizations in two NATO member countries.
incidents.impact: A naval shipbuilder, an aircraft engine manufacturer, and a law enforcement agency were compromised in the campaign.

incidents.victim: California Department of Education (via contractor Educational Testing Service)
incidents.vector: Hackers used a compromised account to repeatedly access Educational Testing Service's secure file transfer platform, which processes statewide assessments for California's K-12 public schools, between May 22 and September 18, 2026.
incidents.impact: Data on all children enrolled in California public schools over the past three years, and former students dating to 2006, was copied, including names, birthdates, addresses, student IDs, demographic data, disability status, and assessment results.

incidents.victim: AOMEI Backupper customers (IT services, telecommunications, and higher education sectors across about a dozen countries including the U.S., Australia, India, and Brazil)
incidents.vector: Attackers repeatedly tampered with AOMEI's update server configuration files in short 5-to-10-minute bursts between April and July 2026, hijacking the software's promotional pop-up channel to deliver the CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor.
incidents.impact: Users who checked for updates during the tampering windows were infected; during one window attackers also coerced machines into sending Windows password hashes to an attacker-controlled server. The true number of victims is likely higher than identified, and already-infected machines remain compromised.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins, and 100+ other e-commerce sites
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking attacker used the AI-driven penetration testing tool Cairn to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation (SQL injection, insecure deserialization, authentication bypass), and web shell deployment across exposed attack dashboards.
incidents.impact: More than 100 sites across the US, Australia, Canada, and Japan were targeted, with at least one confirmed web shell installation; John Deere and SharkNinja said they found no evidence of sensitive data access, while Cummins investigated a potential attack on a third-party vendor's site.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, high technology, hospitality, manufacturing, professional/legal services, government, transportation/logistics, utilities and energy, and wholesale/retail sectors
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploit an authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2026-0257) to establish VPN access, bypass MFA, then pivot to the virtualization layer to disable ESXi security controls and perform offline credential dumping from domain controller virtual disks.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation has continued since June 2026 across numerous industries, with ransomware operators including Qilin, Inc, and Settra deploying ransomware after obtaining domain-wide credentials.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall, and other U.S./European grocery brands)
incidents.vector: Malicious actors caused outages across Ahold Delhaize's IT systems, prompting the company to take systems offline as a precaution; the company has not disclosed the nature of the attack.
incidents.impact: Online ordering and delivery services were disrupted across multiple U.S. and European grocery brands for several days; the company says it has no evidence yet that customer, employee, or partner data was stolen, though the investigation continues. The company suffered a prior breach in 2024 that exposed data of 2.2 million people.

incidents.victim: Romania's Central Depositary (national stock market clearing agency)
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed a database storing personal data of all registered users via the agency's online user portal.
incidents.impact: Names, home addresses, national ID details, emails, phone numbers, and bank account numbers were stolen; officials said no data was altered.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal bankruptcy court system (Bankruptcy Noticing Center)
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted the Bankruptcy Noticing Center platform, which is managed by BAE Systems and used to handle federal bankruptcy case notices.
incidents.impact: The Bankruptcy Noticing Center and other BAE Systems-managed websites were taken offline.

incidents.victim: South Korea National Health Insurance Service
incidents.vector: A National Health Insurance Service employee sold patient data to third parties over a two-year period.
incidents.impact: The employee earned hundreds of thousands of dollars before being fired in July; affected individuals have not yet been notified.

incidents.victim: FirstVDS (Russian VPS provider)
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in the VMmanager virtualization management platform.
incidents.impact: A script was deployed to collect passwords, access keys, configuration files, and crypto-wallet information from compromised servers; the company notified all affected customers.

incidents.victim: Pirate Chain (cryptocurrency)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the network and minted new tokens representing about a fifth of the total supply.
incidents.impact: More than $10 million worth of tokens were minted and quickly laundered out of the network, causing a 25% drop in the token's exchange rate.

incidents.victim: Gamdom (crypto gambling platform)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized connection to an automation server enabled the theft.
incidents.impact: $4.2 million was stolen from the platform.

incidents.victim: Edutest (Russian school testing platform operated by Rosobrnadzor)
incidents.vector: Pro-Ukrainian hacktivist group Black Spark hacked and defaced the Russian school testing platform with anti-Putin and anti-government messages.
incidents.impact: Disruptions to ongoing tests were reported mainly in the Moscow region.
